etymologies.etymologyHTML: From the Middle French progressif, from the Latin prōgressīvus, from prōgredior (perfect participial stem: prōgress-) +‎ -īvus. Displaced native Old English forþgenġe.

definitions.definition: Promoting or favoring progress towards improved conditions or new policies, ideas, or methods.

quote.citation: 2016, Richard Lints, Progressive and Conservative Religious Ideologies, page i:
quote.text: Conservative movements were far more progressive than the standard religious narrative of the decade alleges and the notoriously progressive ethos of the era was far more conservative than our collective memory has recognized.

definitions.definition: (education) Of or relating to progressive education.
(of an income tax or other tax) Increasing in rate as the taxable amount increases.
One with liberal or progressive political beliefs.
